ei.title: The Unexpected Accuracy of First Impressions
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.

det.korean: ① inaccurate → accurate: 설명 못 할 때 '더 정확한(accurate)' 경향
det.analysis:
✅ ① inaccurate → accurate: 원문은 'they tend to be accurate more often'으로, 설명 못 할 때 오히려 '더 정확하다'. inaccurate(부정확한)는 글의 논지와 모순 ← 정답

❌ ② 원문 일치: 즉각적 반응이 가장 참된 해석이라는 내용

❌ ③ 원문 일치: 첫인상이 이성적 서술보다 더 정확할 수 있다는 내용

❌ ④ 원문 일치: 무의식적 직감이 우수한 수행을 보인다는 내용
det.tip: tend to be accurate(정확한) ↔ inaccurate(부정확한)

questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. det.tip: experimental tests of eyewitness testimony = 목격자 증언에 대한 실험

questions.passage: It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just __________ (pop) out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 과거시제 동사 popped
det.analysis: 인용된 발언 'his face just __________ out at me'는 이미 일어난 일을 회상하는 내용이므로 과거시제가 적절. pop은 단모음+단자음으로 끝나 자음을 하나 더 쓰고 -ed를 붙여 popped. pop → popped
det.tip: pop → popped (단모음+단자음 → 자음 중복 + ed)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 즉각적·무의식적 직감이 때로 신중한 추론보다 더 정확하다는 것이 요지
det.analysis:

❌ ② 첫인상은 믿을 수 없음: 본문은 첫인상이 더 정확할 수 있다고 함 — 반대

✅ ③ 무의식적 직감이 더 정확할 때가 있음: 본문의 핵심 주장과 일치 ← 정답

❌ ④ 증언 전혀 신뢰 불가: 본문은 증언 신뢰성 전면 부정이 아님
det.tip: first impression ... more accurate than the reasoned self-narrative

ch: 중요한 결정은 반드시 논리적으로 단계를 밟아 내려야 한다.
